title: Coefficient pushforward of a correspondence
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum and the coefficient conventions,
$A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$; all functors are derived, and we write
$c_2^*$, $c_1^!$ for $Lc_2^*$, $Rc_1^!$. Let
$c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an admissible cohomological
correspondence of [def-trf-correspondence], let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$
and let $u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$ be a correspondence. Let
$b=(b_1,b_2):D\to Y\times_sY$ be a second admissible correspondence. A
*proper pushforward diagram* $(f,g):(C,c)\to(D,b)$ consists of proper
morphisms

$$
f:X\longrightarrow Y,\qquad g:C\longrightarrow D,
\qquad b_ig=fc_i\quad(i=1,2).
$$

No Cartesian condition is imposed on either leg square
$(c_i,g,b_i,f)$, and $X,Y,C,D$ need not be proper over $s$. Put
$K'=Rf_*K$. Write $\eta_g:\operatorname{id}\to Rg_*g^*$ and
$\varepsilon_f:f^*Rf_*\to\operatorname{id}$ for the unit and counit of
the ordinary adjunctions, and $\varepsilon_{c_1}:Rc_{1!}c_1^!\to\operatorname{id}$
for the counit of $Rc_{1!}\dashv c_1^!$, all as in [fix-prop-adjunctions].

1. *The ordinary half.* Let
$$
\begin{aligned}
\gamma:b_2^*K'
&\xrightarrow{\ \eta_g\ }Rg_*g^*b_2^*Rf_*K
= Rg_*c_2^*f^*Rf_*K\\
&\xrightarrow{\ Rg_*c_2^*\varepsilon_f\ }Rg_*c_2^*K,
\end{aligned}
$$
the equality being the pullback composition $g^*b_2^*=(b_2g)^*=(fc_2)^*=c_2^*f^*$.
1. *The exceptional half.* Since $f$ and $g$ are proper,
$Rf_*=Rf_!$ and $Rg_*=Rg_!$ ([prop-functor-package], clause (3)), and the
composition law of [thm-sf-comp-composition] applied to $b_1g=fc_1$ gives
$\Xi_1:Rb_{1!}Rg_*\cong R(b_1g)_!=R(fc_1)_!\cong Rf_!Rc_{1!}$. Let
$$
\delta:Rg_*c_1^!K\longrightarrow b_1^!K'
$$
be the exceptional adjoint (for $Rb_{1!}\dashv b_1^!$) of
$$
Rb_{1!}Rg_*c_1^!K\xrightarrow{\ \Xi_1\ }Rf_!Rc_{1!}c_1^!K
\xrightarrow{\ Rf_!\varepsilon_{c_1}\ }Rf_!K=K'.
$$
1. The *coefficient pushforward* of $u$ is
$$
[f,g]_!u:=\delta\circ Rg_*u\circ\gamma:\
b_2^*K'\longrightarrow b_1^!K',
$$
a correspondence on $(Y,K')$ supported on $b$.
1. *The induced map of fixed schemes.* Let $F_c=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$
and $F_b=\operatorname{Fix}(b)$ be the fixed schemes of
[def-trf-fixed-scheme], with projections $i_c:F_c\to C$, $d_c:F_c\to X$
and $i_b:F_b\to D$, $d_b:F_b\to Y$. Since
$b\,g\,i_c=(f\times f)\,c\,i_c=(f\times f)\Delta_Xd_c=\Delta_Y\,f\,d_c$,
the universal property of $F_b=D\times_{Y\times_sY,\Delta_Y}Y$ gives a
unique morphism
$$
h:F_c\longrightarrow F_b,\qquad i_bh=g\,i_c,\qquad d_bh=f\,d_c .
$$

*The Cartesian case.* Neither construction uses a Cartesian
square, but they reduce to the familiar maps when the squares are
Cartesian. The recipe for $\gamma$ is the recipe of the exchange
$\operatorname{Ex}_*$ of [def-exchange-projection] (the adjoint of the
counit composed with the identification of pullbacks); so if
$(c_2,g,b_2,f)$ is Cartesian, $\gamma=\operatorname{Ex}_*$ is the proper
base-change isomorphism $b_2^*Rf_*\cong Rg_*c_2^*$ of
[prop-functor-package], clause (4). The map $\delta$ is the exchange map
of [def-trf-admissibility] formed from the composition law and the
exceptional counits; if $(c_1,g,b_1,f)$ is Cartesian, it is inverse to the
dual base-change isomorphism $b_1^!Rf_*\cong Rg_*c_1^!$ of
[thm-sf-dual-base-change] (applied with $b_1$ as the exceptional map and
$f$ as the proper map). Indeed, the latter is the mate of
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$, and $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is compatible with the
composition law ([fix-lem-exchanges], item 4) and with the adjunctions
([fix-prop-adjunctions], item 4), so the two mates are mutually inverse.

split_report.summary: Split the definition by recording its nine existing statement dependencies; no new nodes. Checked the main-20261015 definition and every cited statement, including the constructible finite-coefficient domains. The ordinary half is a unit-pullback-comparison-counit composite; the exceptional half is the adjunction transpose of the displayed compact-support composite. The fixed-scheme map is the explicit pullback lift. In the Cartesian specialization the existing proper and dual base-change statements apply with the specified labels. Recorded seven real Mathlib searches, including a second semantic phrasing; no match. The source Lean definitions require additional supplied GeometricOperations data and do not establish the final Cartesian characterization, so they do not attach the entire item.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the main-20261015 definition, clauses 1 (ordinary half), 2 (exceptional half), 3 (coefficient composite), 4 (fixed-scheme lift), and its Cartesian-case paragraph. The same construction occurs in the blueprint unit sketch sk-d-proper-pushforward, now recorded in same_as; the detailed node additionally spells out the fixed-scheme equations and Cartesian comparison. Removed the obsolete Varshavsky parenthetical and the old forward pointer on properness to use blueprint_update.statement verbatim. All blueprint_update and import metadata remain unchanged.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q57-2c9e29e53 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, all nine cited statements (def-trf-correspondence, fix-prop-adjunctions 1-4, prop-functor-package 3-4, thm-sf-comp-composition, def-trf-fixed-scheme, def-exchange-projection, def-trf-admissibility, thm-sf-dual-base-change, fix-lem-exchanges 4), the master and main-20261015 blueprint files, the unit sketch, Varshavsky math/0505564 §1.1.6, the slopmaster2 file ProperPushforward.lean lines 100-239, and every citer. The statement matches blueprint_update and the main-20261015 text exactly. It only drops the Varshavsky parenthetical and the forward pointer, so nothing is weakened. Checked each clause: gamma is unit of g, then the leg identification, then the counit of f. delta is the b1-transpose of Xi1 followed by Rf_! eps_{c1}. Both typecheck on D^b_ctf, using the constructible exceptional adjunction of def-trf-admissibility and not an ambient adjoint. The composite is elementary. h is the lift into the fibre product F_b, from b g i_c = Delta_Y f d_c. Cartesian paragraph: with the substitutions (C,X,D,Y,c2,f,g,b2) and (C,D,X,Y,c1,b1,g,f), gamma equals Ex_*, which prop-functor-package (4) makes an isomorphism. delta has the type of the conjugate of Ex_! and is inverse to the dual base change via the composition compatibility. These claims are true and no citer uses them; I accept them as a verbatim remark. Recipes match Varshavsky 1.1.6(ii) (legs swapped under the shriek adjunction) and slopmaster2 pushforwardCoeffUnit/Counit/fixMap on the ctf domain. That Lean makes f an s-morphism (f_comp); the DAG node leaves this implicit in the k-scheme convention. Edge cases checked: identity diagram gives u back, K=0, empty supports, the point target reproduces the global operator, and non-Cartesian legs. No new nodes; sk-d-proper-pushforward is correctly in same_as; no SGA; no fixes needed.
